flags.headline: MARA downgraded RED->AMBER -- shares +8.97% on a new $9.8B-adjacent AI power buildout, a second straight up day, though Morgan Stanley's $5.50 PT / Underweight and BTC-leverage risk remain live
flags.detail: MARA gained 8.97% to $11.66 (prev close $10.70), extending Monday's +9.2% pop to $11.67. The driver is a newly announced 1,200-acre powered site in Matagorda County, Texas (from HIF USA, co-developed with Starwood Digital Ventures) delivering 1 GW of grid capacity by 2027 and 2 GW by 2028 for Bitcoin mining and HPC/AI -- lifting MARA's total potential power capacity toward ~4.8 GW alongside the existing Long Ridge deal. This is a direct, positive read on the thesis's AI/HPC-diversification catalyst. Piper Sandler still trimmed its PT to $13 (from $16, kept Overweight) citing AI data-center demand offsetting sector-wide crypto/AI weakness -- constructive, not bearish. Morgan Stanley's bearish $5.50 PT (07-16) has not been refreshed but the balance of this week's news flow is clearly positive. Downgrading from RED to AMBER: the acute price-decline/downgrade story has reversed, but MARA remains a leveraged, unprofitable bet on Bitcoin (down 17.9% over the past month, -40.2% YoY) so this stays on watch rather than resolving to green.
flags.thesis_link: Positive read against MARA key_catalyst #1 (Long Ridge/AI-HPC power diversification reducing crypto-price dependency) materializing via the new Texas site; key_risk #1/#3 (leveraged BTC derivative, existential risk if crypto turns) remains the reason this stays AMBER rather than green. Persisting since 2026-06-30 (originally flagged RED).

evidence.source: The Motley Fool -- Why Mara Holdings Stock Crushed the Market on Monday
ts2.tech -- MARA Holdings shares climb 9% following rival AI agreements

flags.headline: STLD new AMBER -- shares down on Q2 print despite higher earnings, as an aluminum-segment impairment and startup losses overshadow record steel shipments
flags.detail: Steel Dynamics reported Q2 2026 net income of $534M ($3.69/share) on $6.1B net sales and record steel shipments of 3.7M tons after Monday's close, but shares fell (-2.23% intraday per the data drop to $230.28; contemporaneous coverage cited as much as -4.3%) on a $16M non-cash impairment tied to relocating a planned aluminum recycled-slab center from Arizona to Mississippi, plus ongoing aluminum startup losses and softer steel-fabrication profitability. evidence.source: StockTitan -- Steel Dynamics Falls After Q2 Release Despite Higher Earnings
